evidence.mechanism: shot-08s: six oxblood arms carry hairline side branches, and the defect letters bunch at the centre instead of trailing the tip; by shot-20s the arms are densely hatched with small tip arrowheads.
evidence.ambition: shot-20s: one flat vector layer over a radial clay gradient, six arms with hatched side branches and a centred glyph clump; no shading, material or second rendering pass is visible.
evidence.craft: shot-08s: letters overlap into an illegible knot at the centre and the arrowhead tips are crude triangles; shot-02s rose-clay and oxblood palette is clean with hairline ridges.
evidence.distinctness: shot-02s: centred six-point oxblood star on rose-clay; by shot-08s it reads as a snowflake outline, close to the brief's own discarded idea, though it shares no tiling look with the recent night.
evidence.polish: shot-02s: composed and centred, but the tip does not fill the frame as storyboarded; shot-20s resolves to the full figure with more branches than at 2s, so the loop develops.

pairwise_justification: Penrose at its 20s frame fills the triangle with dense ochre kites and rust darts; tonight's sparse oxblood star with a clumped glyph centre loses the head-to-head vote on density.

critique.change: At shot-08s and shot-20s, place each glyph of 'defect' at one fixed distance behind the moving tip and grow exactly one side arm from each letter, so the lag is seen instead of a centred clump.
At shot-02s, scale the star so the tip fills the frame as storyboarded and thin the arm ridges as the tip speeds up, so the V-R sharpness lock shows on screen instead of as HUD numbers.
Remove the top-left title and bottom-left V/R readout, which tell the mechanism in text, and use the freed space for an arm-length gradient between older and newer side branches.
